title: Use of technology for greater road safety discussed at IIT Madras
excerpt: Kolkata, Nov 4 (IANS) The use of Geospatial data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enable advanced road safety interventions came up for discussion during a fireside chat with Justice Abhay Manohar Sapre, former judge, Supreme Court of India, and chairman, Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety (SCCoRS), and Sanjay Bandopadhyay, member, SCCoRS at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras on Wednesday. The event brought together students, practitioners and innovators, who explored India's road safety challenges and the role of technology in addressing them. The key causes of road crashes, including overspeeding, drunk driving, wrong-side driving, jumping red lights, mobile phone use while driving, unsafe overtaking and driver fatigue and stress, were highlighted by Justice Sapre. He also spoke on the importance of applying first-principles thinking to develop effective solutions. Custom Ad: Multiplex The Road Safety Innovation Hub, developed by the Government of Tamil Nadu with RBG Labs, was also introduced during the session as a platform for students, researchers and entrepreneurs to share, test and advance their ideas. The Road Safety Innovation Hub often works alongside academic partners like the Centre of Excellence for Road Safety at IIT Madras to design, test, and deploy new technologies and data-driven solutions for safer roads. Its core focus area is creating data-backed safety interventions, smart mobility tools, low-cost engineering fixes, and emerging safety technologies to reduce traffic crashes and fatalities. It aligns with similar state and national deep-tech frameworks in India — such as Odisha's design-thinking capacity programs and IIT Delhi's Bharat Safety initiative — to scale tech-driven road safety. According to data shared in Parliament by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), 1,77,177 people were killed in road accidents in India in 2024. This was a 2.3% increase from the previous year. This effectively means that nearly 485 people die due to road accidents in India every day, and the toll is about 20 per hour. Data reveals that the number of deaths has gone up over the years. While 1,68,491 people were killed in 2022, the toll was 1,72,890 in 2023. About 46.2% of those killed are two-wheeler riders, while 20.6% are pedestrians. About 66.1% of those killed are in the productive age group of 18 to 45 years, while those aged between 18 and 60 make up 83.3%. --IANS jg/dan

title: Telangana HC suspends Jangaon collector’s order over alleged AI-generated findings
excerpt: HYDERABAD: The Telangana High Court on Tuesday expressed concern over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated platforms by district administrations to dispose of public grievance petitions without properly examining the facts or verifying whether the issues raised had been resolved. Justice N V Shravan Kumar took exception to the Jangaon collector’s alleged reliance […]HYDERABAD: The Telangana High Court on Tuesday expressed concern over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated platforms by district administrations to dispose of public grievance petitions without properly examining the facts or verifying whether the issues raised had been resolved. Justice N V Shravan Kumar took exception to the Jangaon collector’s alleged reliance on AI-generated material while passing an order in a revenue dispute. The court questioned how an authority could decide matters concerning property rights without verifying the facts and hearing the affected parties. The judge was hearing a writ petition filed by Medipalli Komuraiah of Peddamdur village in Devaruppula mandal of Jangaon district. He challenged the collector’s order dated September 8, alleging that it had been passed without considering his contentions. Court seeks explanation on action against officials Suspending the collector’s September 8 order, the High Court sought an explanation from Advocate-General A Sudarshan Reddy on the action proposed against officials for the alleged lapses. The court also directed the Advocate-General to inform it of the steps taken in the matter. Petitioner alleges mechanical disposal of revenue grievance According to the petitioner’s counsel, M Madhava Reddy, the collector passed an order on a grievance submitted by the opposite parties in a revenue-related dispute without hearing Komuraiah’s submissions. The counsel told the court that the order had caused serious hardship to the petitioner. He further alleged that officials had mechanically relied on AI tools without examining the underlying facts or applying their own mind. The court’s observations came amid concerns over the use of automated systems in administrative decision-making, particularly in matters involving property rights and individual grievances. ]]>

title: Govt aims to make Maharashtra a global hub for future mobility, says CM Fadnavis
excerpt: Pune, Nov 4 (IANS) Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday that the state government aims to transform the state from being just a national automotive hub into a global hub for future mobility. Moving from 'Make in Maharashtra' to 'Innovate in Maharashtra', the state government is actively promoting research, engineering, technology development, and innovations alongside manufacturing. The Chief Minister was speaking at the launch of Mercedes-Benz's state-of-the-art Electric GLC vehicle at Chakan. He highlighted that a massive automotive industry cluster has developed in the Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad regions, with Maharashtra contributing more than 20 per cent to India's total motor vehicle production. Custom Ad: Multiplex "The state's ambition is not limited to vehicle assembly alone but extends to achieving global leadership in electric vehicles (EVs), battery technology, power electronics, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, automobile software, design, and research and development (R&D)." The Chief Minister urged Mercedes-Benz to manufacture from Chakan for both Asian and global markets alongside the Indian domestic market, while prioritising Maharashtra for future battery technology, software engineering, and mobility research. Under the state's Electric Vehicle Policy, a target of 30 per cent EV adoption in new vehicle registrations has been set by 2030, CM Fadnavis said, adding that fast-charging infrastructure along highways, sustainable mobility corridors along the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and Samruddhi Mahamarg, and battery recycling initiatives are actively being promoted. The Chief Minister noted that future vehicles will no longer merely be four-wheel transportation, but rather an integrated mobility platform combined with computers, energy systems, and artificial intelligence. Maharashtra is fully prepared to lead this transformation, he added. He also said that connectivity to global markets will be enhanced further through the Navi Mumbai International Airport, the proposed Pune-Purandar Airport, and the Vadhavan Port. Driven by a large market, a robust manufacturing ecosystem, skilled engineers, and advanced technology, Maharashtra has emerged as a premier investment destination. He said that around 650 customers expressed interest in the Electric GLC vehicle within just 36 hours. Manufacturing, research, and innovation are being actively developed from Maharashtra for the world, the Chief Minister added. "Mercedes-Benz's Chakan plant with an investment of Rs 3,200 crore has provided direct employment to around 1,200 people, while creating job opportunities for nearly 18,000 individuals through supplier networks and service sectors. The rollout of the state-of-the-art Electric GLC from this plant within ten years of its expansion stands as a testament to the state's industrial and technological progress," he said. Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar said that Mercedes-Benz has contributed significantly to Maharashtra's industrial growth over the past three decades. "The commencement of localised production for electric vehicles marks a critical milestone in the state's industrial development. This manufacturing effort—combining electrical energy, artificial intelligence, and eco-friendly manufacturing technologies—shows that Pune is ready for future mobility systems." Former Deputy CM late Ajit Pawar's vision of empowering Maharashtra in future transportation through world-class EV manufacturing and technology in Pune district is being realised, she noted. She emphasised the state government's commitment to promoting modern mobility technology and economic growth, noting that this initiative complements Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of 'Viksit Bharat 2047'. She urged global industrial groups to collaborate on water conservation, groundwater research, and water security in drought-prone areas of Maharashtra. As the Guardian Minister of Pune, Sunetra Pawar assured full cooperation to all stakeholders in the industrial sector, reaffirming that the state government stands firmly behind industries to address their challenges. Martin Brudermuller (Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Mercedes-Benz Group AG), Ola Kallenius (Chairman of the Board of Management and Global Head, Mercedes-Benz Group AG), and Jorg Burzer (Member of the Board of Management and CTO) shared their remarks. Santosh Iyer, Managing Director of Mercedes-Benz India, provided an introductory overview of the company's progress over the past thirty years and expressed appreciation for the state government's strong support. --IANS sj/khz
